title: Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture (Conjecture 1.5)
statement_text: For every tree $T$ and complete graph $K$, there is an integer $c$ such that if $G$ is a graph containing neither $T$ nor $K$ as an induced subgraph, then $\chi(G) \leq c$.
context_text: This conjecture is invoked as the graph-theoretic motivation for the paper's study of induced restrictions in binary matroids, where matroids $I_t$ play the role of trees and projective geometries $PG(t-1,2)$ play the role of cliques. The paper notes the conjecture remains open in general, though proved for many specific trees $T$.
paper_contribution: Theorem 1.3 refutes the matroidal analogue of this conjecture by showing that for every integer $k$ there exists a matroid $M \in \mathcal{E}_3$ containing neither $I_3$ nor $F_7$ as an induced restriction with $\chi(M) \geq k$, establishing that bounding $\chi$ by excluding a fixed $I_s$ and a fixed $PG(t-1,2)$ as induced restrictions is impossible in general.
paper_title: The structure of binary matroids with no induced claw or Fano plane restriction

title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: For all $s \geq 1$ there exists an integer $k$ such that if $M$ is a simple binary matroid with no induced $I_s$-restriction or $PG(1, 2)$-restriction, then $\chi(M) \leq k$.
context_text: Here a simple binary matroid is a pair $M=(E,G)$ where $G$ is a finite-dimensional binary projective geometry $\mathrm{PG}(n-1,2)$ (the nonzero vectors of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with $n$ the dimension of $M$) and $E\subseteq G$ is the ground set. $M$ contains $N=(F,G')$ as a restriction if there is a linear injection $\varphi:G'\to G$ with $\varphi(F)\subseteq E$, and as an induced restriction if moreover $\varphi(F)=E\cap\varphi(G')$; equivalently, an induced restriction is $M$ restricted to a flat. $\mathrm{PG}(t-1,2)$ also denotes the matroid whose ground set is the whole geometry; in particular $\mathrm{PG}(1,2)$ is a triangle (three points $x,y,x+y$), the analogue of a clique $K_3$. $I_s$ is the $s$-dimensional matroid whose ground set is a basis of $s$ elements, the analogue of a tree; $I_3$ is called a claw. The critical number $\chi(M)$ of an $n$-dimensional $M$ is the least $k$ such that $G\setminus E$ contains a projective geometry of dimension $n-k$; it is the matroid analogue of the chromatic number, and $\chi(M(G))=\lceil\log_2\chi(G)\rceil$ for cycle matroids of graphs. The natural matroid analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (excluding $I_s$ and $\mathrm{PG}(t-1,2)$ bounds $\chi$) fails: the authors construct matroids with no induced $I_3$ or Fano plane $F_7=\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$ restriction and arbitrarily large critical number. They conjecture that excluding a triangle ($t=2$) restores a bound. They show the conjecture is easy for $s\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $k=1$ suffices, but new ideas are needed for larger $s$. The graph analogue (excluding an induced tree $T$ and a triangle) is easy for stars but open in general. Matroid theory rather than graph theory.
paper_title: The structure of binary matroids with no induced claw or Fano plane restriction
